ordered_diagnoses: Sjögren's Syndrome with Central Nervous System Involvement

s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of neurological deficits with evidence of inflammation and white matter changes
salient_findings: Mild aphasia and confusion
Sudden-onset right leg weakness
Mild headache and right facial droop
Extensive white matter changes on MRI
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level
key_facts: History of well-controlled hypertension and hyperlipidemia
On methotrexate and sulfasalazine treatment
Developed mild aphasia and confusion lasting several hours
Right leg weakness resolved within 2 days
Presented with mild headache and right facial droop
Neurological examination revealed paraphasic errors and word-finding difficulty
Mild right nasolabial flattening and bilateral upgoing plantars
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level
High titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody
CSF analysis showed 12/µL white blood cell count and 4 oligoclonal bands
MRI Brain showed extensive white matter changes with enhancement along the arachnoid surface

shortlist: Sjögren's Syndrome with Central Nervous System Involvement

shortlist.label: Multiple Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of neurological deficits with evidence of inflammation and white matter changes, CSF analysis showed 4 oligoclonal bands

shortlist.label: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
shortlist.why_kept: History of optic neuritis and transverse myelitis-like episodes, presence of oligoclonal bands in CSF

shortlist.label: Primary Central Nervous System Vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Evidence of inflammation and white matter changes on MRI, presence of elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level

shortlist.label: Sjögren's Syndrome with Central Nervous System Involvement
shortlist.why_kept: History of autoimmune disorders, presence of lymphocytes and plasma cells in brain biopsy, and elevated cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody

shortlist.label: Neurosarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of non-caseating granulomas in brain biopsy, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level, and history of autoimmune disorders

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of relapsing neurological symptoms (mild aphasia and confusion, right leg weakness, and right facial droop) with complete or partial resolution, along with the presence of oligoclonal bands in the CSF and extensive white matter changes on MRI, is highly suggestive of Multiple Sclerosis.

rejected.label: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
rejected.why: The absence of optic neuritis and the presence of oligoclonal bands in the CSF make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Primary Central Nervous System Vasculitis
rejected.why: The brain biopsy did not show evidence of vasculitis, and the MRI findings are not typical for this condition.

rejected.label: Sjögren's Syndrome with Central Nervous System Involvement
rejected.why: There is no mention of symptoms or laboratory findings suggestive of Sjögren's Syndrome, such as dry eyes or mouth, or positive anti-SSA/Ro or anti-SSB/La antibodies.

rejected.label: Neurosarcoidosis
rejected.why: The brain biopsy did not show non-caseating granulomas, which are characteristic of sarcoidosis, and there is no other evidence of systemic sarcoidosis, such as pulmonary nodules on chest CT.
